`13dc5dcb6271112b241985a16142e7a2`.
Structured side: `env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/protection_claims_desk/protection.extended.yaml`
and `task_tools.py`. Blind phase frozen first, at
`audits/runtime_context/protection_claims_desk/1.md`.

**Entry conditions (checked and cited, not re-run).** The source-layer verdict for this difficulty is PASS
on both tasks across all four relationships (`audits/policy_task/protection_claims_desk/`). The gate
snapshot supplied with the brief — `check_docs.py … protection` → `DOCS OK (docs=79 roles={'policy': 15,
'hub': 8, 'facet': 9, 'factor': 39, 'baseline': 8}; required quantitative keys=149 task_tools=8
prerequisite edges=6)`, and `check_traceability.py … protection_claims_desk` → `TRACEABILITY OK` with

tool-shaped DB access path were both supplied; `initial_state` was never read as a document during the
blind phase. No input is missing.

**Division of labour with the sibling file.** The base-policy sweep (15 of 15), the measures (3 of 3), the

Every `baseline.rule` is carried complete in its own `baseline`-role document, with the policy's own

#### A1. `protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing` → `working_out_a_premium_instalment`

Source `baseline.rule`: the instalment is the plan's monthly premium; the trading record read over the last
three months; no trading discount; no claims loading; no terms discount; "the plan's monthly premium
adjusted once by the loadings and discounts combined into a single rate, taken to the cent and never below
nothing". All six sentences are in the document, with the source's own anti-compounding sentence carried
verbatim in substance — "The loading and the discounts are first combined into one rate and the plan's
monthly premium is adjusted once by that rate; they do not act one after another on the figure the previous
one left" — and its restatement "The single rate is 100 percent, raised by the loading and lowered by each
discount, and the plan's monthly premium is taken at that rate once". Product figure named: "The plan's
monthly premium is the figure recorded against that plan", rendered in `premium_tariff_schedule` (39.00 for
ShieldCare Business Fleet Protection). The `overwrite` this policy declares on `protection_premium_billing`
is written as retired in `how_premium_is_billed_and_applied` cl. 2 and its replacement is not restated
there (see `policy_kb/…/0.md` §C).

The rule's scope: the source reads "The instalment for a premium period **on a plan held on instalments**",
with no limb confining it to the fleet tier, and the KB reads "For a premium period on a **Northbeam
ShieldCare Protection Plan held on instalments**" / "An instalment falls due for each premium period on a
Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan held on instalments". **Faithful.** The word "fleet" appears in the
policy id and in the tool identifier `settle_fleet_invoice_2818623b` (which the hub must name), and nowhere
in any rule; the KB is right not to narrow it, and the task rationales that say otherwise are not a source.
A domain consequence is recorded as P5 in `policy_kb/…/0.md`.

### B. Task 1's three prerequisite edges — the resolution basis

The register of all six edges, with the verbatim-occurrence proof, is in `policy_kb/…/0.md` §F. All three of
task 1's edges are `form: state`, each carried verbatim in the hub of the problem it blocks, each occurring
exactly once across all 385 published documents, each with its ordering connective and hard strength intact.
Note that two of them sit as **separate sentences of one hub's own rule** — which is the source's own shape,
since both point at the same blocked problem.

- Edge 5 (`..._fleet_invoice_settlement` waits on `..._fleet_instalment_billing`). Sentence, in
  `settling_a_premium_invoice_on_a_plan`: "The amount the account settles is fixed only after every premium
  period the plan has reached stands billed on it." Words of the state: *a premium period the plan has
  reached*, *stands billed on it*. Depended-on rule, in `billing_a_premium_instalment_period`: "An
  instalment falls due for each premium period on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan held on
  instalments. The entry raises the premium the customer still owes on that plan by the amount billed." The
  records supply which period: the newest `protection_premium_charge` runs `period_start 2026-08-10` /
  `period_end 2026-09-09`, so at `frozen_time` 2026-09-16 the period opening 2026-09-10 has been reached and
  carries no charge. Resolvable at the same strength from the sentence + the depended-on rule + the records.
- Edge 6 (`..._fleet_invoice_settlement` waits on `..._claim_excess_settlement`). Sentence, in the same
  hub: "The premium on the plan is taken only once a payment against the claim excess stands received on the
  plan for every claim the plan has settled by replacement." Words: *a payment against the claim excess*,
  *stands received on the plan*, over the set *every claim the plan has settled by replacement*.
  Depended-on rule, in `settling_the_excess_standing_against_a_claim`: "What is then taken is recorded as an
  excess payment against that claim, and the claim excess still owed on the plan falls by the amount paid."
  Records: `SC-2026-70431` carries a `protection_claim_decision` of `approved_replacement` with
  `settlement_basis: 'replacement'`, and no `protection_deductible_payment` stands anywhere in the 49-row
  ledger. Resolvable at the same strength.
- Edge 4 (`..._claim_excess_settlement` waits on `..._claim_excess_charge`). Sentence, in
  `settling_the_excess_standing_against_a_claim`: "What the account settles on a claim excess is fixed only
  after that excess stands billed on the plan." Words: *that excess*, *stands billed on the plan*.
  Depended-on rule, in `billing_the_excess_on_an_approved_claim`: "An excess is owed by the customer on an
  approved claim under a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan, and it is billed once for that claim. The
  entry raises the claim excess the customer still owes on that plan by the amount billed." Records: no
  `protection_deductible_charge` on the plan, `deductible_outstanding` 0.00. Resolvable at the same strength.

**The depended-on side never discloses who waits on it.**
`billing_a_premium_instalment_period` and `billing_the_excess_on_an_approved_claim` each carry only their
own rule and no prerequisite sentence at all (neither is blocked by anything);
`settling_the_excess_standing_against_a_claim` carries only the sentence that blocks *it*, not the one by
which the invoice settlement waits on it. Confirmed by the one-occurrence count.

## kb_to_source

### 1. Nothing added as procedure

The mechanical sweeps recorded in `policy_kb/…/0.md` `kb_to_source` §1 cover the whole product corpus and
apply here unchanged: no added confirmation, review, notification, re-check, escalation or follow-up step
anywhere in the 79 documents, and no route phrasing of any kind.

### 2. One addition that changes the domain — recorded as RED (this task's own factor)

`docs/protection/the_allowance_a_managed_care_agreement_carries_c6a3dea7.json`, content line 9:

> `| such an agreement, one carrying at least 1 included visit in its term, and no visit stands drawn on it inside that time | 30.00 |`

The source states no such threshold. Its ladder tier and its rule sentence both read:

> `factors[managed_care_allowance].ladder[1].when`: "the profile holds such an agreement and no visit
> stands drawn on it inside that time"
> `rule`: "it is thirty dollars where the profile holds such an agreement and no visit stands drawn on it
> inside that time"

The nearest antecedent of "such an agreement" is tier 1's "a care agreement whose included visits run to
twelve or more in its term". So on the source's normative prose, tier 2 reaches only a 12-or-more
agreement; on the KB's, it reaches any care agreement carrying at least one included visit. The KB asserts
the widened reading twice more:

> lines 15–16: "one carrying 11 included visits is not, and with no visit drawn inside that time it
> reaches the middle row at 30.00"
> line 26: `| 6 | no | 30.00 |`

Neither an 11-visit nor a 6-visit agreement reaching 30.00 has any home in the source's rule or ladder. The
figure `1` exists in the source **only** in the executable binding:

```
care_allowance: "K('care_allowance_full_usd') if ((care_visits or 0) >= K('care_visits_threshold') and care_visits_drawn >= 1)
                 else (K('care_allowance_part_usd') if ((care_visits or 0) >= 1 and care_visits_drawn <= 0) else 0.0)"
```

So the KB has matched the binding and, in doing so, has stated in figures a threshold its normative source
never states, widening a tier's reach on the reading a careful reader of the source's prose would take. The
underlying disagreement is between the source's own prose and its own binding, which is a policy-side
defect; the KB's silent resolution of it in the binding's favour is the document-side defect recorded here.

**Domain reach of the widening.** The published TechWorks entitlement schedule
(`docs/service/…included_visits_and_annual_care_terms…`, column "Included visits per term") gives 0 for In
Store Bench Service, 1 for Standard Home Installation, 2 for Home Theatre Calibration, 1 for Appliance
Install and Haul Away, 4 for Business On Site Deployment and 12 for Managed IT Care Annual. So exactly one
service reaches tier 1 either way, and the widening bites on the four services carrying 1 to 4 visits: a
profile holding only one of those, with no visit drawn inside the year, gets 30.00 on the KB's reading and
nothing on the source prose's. **This difficulty's own task 0 profile is such a case** — it holds a
`TechWorks Appliance Install and Haul Away` agreement (1 included visit per term) with no visit drawn —
though task 0 computes no excess, so nothing is scored on it.

**It changes no scored number on either task.** Task 1's profile holds a `TechWorks Managed IT Care Annual`
agreement whose term carries 12 included visits, with two `service_visit_consume` rows inside the year
(2026-05-18, 2026-08-06), so tier 1 governs and the allowance is 60.00 on every reading.

### 3. The compute's hard-coded variant name — checked, and the KB is on the right side

The source binding for the same factor names one product variant that no rule mentions:

```
care_agreement_job: "CFIELD('service','service_agreement_id', variant_name='TechWorks Managed IT Care Annual')"
care_visits:        "CPARAM('service','included_visits_per_term', status='scheduled')"
```

The rule and the ladder speak only of "a care agreement whose included visits run to twelve or more in its
term", and the KB renders exactly that, naming the product line by its official name ("under Northbeam
TechWorks Installation and Repair") and the record kinds it reads, and **not** the variant. That is the
faithful rendering, and it is the one this audit endorses.

Whether the divergence can change an answer was tested rather than assumed, on both tasks' worlds:

- **Task 1:** `find_service_agreements` returns exactly one agreement, `701cb1ea…`, and it *is*
  `TechWorks Managed IT Care Annual`. Variant-scoped and rule-scoped readings select the same agreement, the
  same 12 visits and the same two drawn visits. Allowance 60.00 either way. No effect.
- **Task 0:** no excess is computed at all (the excess on `SC-2026-88413` stands billed at 75.00 on
  2026-09-08 and paid on 2026-09-09), so the factor is never reached. No effect.
- **Across the domain:** on tier 1 the two readings coincide, because the TechWorks schedule gives 12
  included visits per term to `TechWorks Managed IT Care Annual` alone. They come apart only on tier 2 —
  and only because of the widening in §2. The two findings therefore compound: it is the KB's added "at
  least 1 included visit" clause that opens the very gap between the KB and a variant-scoped compute that
  the render report warned of. Without it, tier 2 would also be confined to 12-or-more agreements and the
  hard-coded variant would be harmless throughout.

## Further problems found (outside the three verdict categories)

The full list of policy-side and render-side problems is recorded once, at
`audits/policy_kb/protection_claims_desk/0.md` under "Further problems found" (P1–P10). Those bearing on
task 1 are:

- **P4** — `the_price_of_a_period_billed_in_advance` prints 41.34 beside a monthly premium of 39.00, which
  is this task's scored instalment beside this plan's own monthly premium; and
  `the_discount_earned_by_the_trading_record`'s case row "18400.00 | active | 6 percent" sits 20.00 from
  this task's actual merchandise total of 18420.00, on the same tier. Render-side leak risk.
- **P5** — `protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing`'s rule is general rather than fleet-confined, which the
  KB renders faithfully; the domain consequence is that it overlaps
  `protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement`'s pricing of a period on a non-fleet plan. Policy side.
- **P6** — the prose-versus-binding class: `managed_care_allowance`'s "such an agreement" is finding B1;
  `household_excess_on_food`'s "stands unsettled" is its harmless twin. Policy side in origin.
- **P7** — `loading_window_counted`'s "from the month the cover was most recently put back" names a month
  rather than a day, in the source's own words and the KB's. Immaterial here (the reinstatement stands
  2026-02-10 and both counted claims are filed in March and August 2026). Policy side.
- **P8** — `service_agreements.701cb1ea…` carries `visits_remaining: 9` while its own ledger grants 12 and
  consumes 2, netting to 10. Recorded because a solver who reached for that field instead of the TechWorks
  entitlement schedule would fall out of tier 1 and, visits being drawn inside the year, out of tier 2 too,
  reaching no allowance and an excess of 262.50 instead of 202.50. The source binding uses the variant
  parameter and the KB's "the included visits its term carries" points at the term's entitlement rather than
  the remainder, so the corpus is on the right side of it. Policy side.
- **New here, P11** — the KB states no billing-day rule for an instalment plan, because the clause that had
  one is retired by this very policy's `overwrite` on `protection_premium_billing`, and
  `how_premium_is_billed_and_applied` cl. 2 reports it as no longer in force with the replacement not
  restated there. Edge 5 nevertheless turns on "every premium period the plan has reached", which the reader
  must fix from the pattern of the plan's own charges (the 10th of each month). This is faithful — the source
  has no such rule either, and its own `prerequisite_closure` resolves the period from the ledger the same
  way — and the ledger makes it unambiguous on this world. Recorded as a policy-side note about how thin the
  join is, not as a document defect.

## Step 4 — settling the problems

- **Never accommodate in reverse.** B1 is reported as a defect of the document. Where the document and the
  policy conflict, the policy is the faithful side; here the policy's own prose and its own binding conflict
  with each other, which is reported as such rather than resolved in the document's favour.
- **Never dissolve a contradiction by hiding one side.** No finding proposes that a document state one of
  two conflicting bases and drop the other.
- **Report policy-side problems without letting them change this skill's verdict.** P5–P8 and P11 are
  policy-side and are recorded with their evidence; this skill's verdict rests only on the document-side
  evidence.
- **Never recommend more than the source states.** Nothing above proposes naming a tool, a resolving
  problem or a route, and nothing proposes deleting a prerequisite sentence.
- **Nothing is attributed to a solving agent.**
